Finding a Roofing Company in Little Elm, Texas

Most Little Elm roofs went up in the last 25 years, as the lake town grew more than tenfold. Call one free number, any hour, to be connected with an independent roofing company that serves Little Elm.

A lake town that grew in one generation

Choosing a roofing company in Little Elm usually means dealing with a roof that is younger than you might think. The town counted 3,646 people in 2000, 25,898 in 2010 and 46,453 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimated 58,496 by mid-2023.

Little Elm sits on the northern and eastern shores of Lewisville Lake, with 66 miles of shoreline by the town's economic development count. KERA reported in 2019 that the town's population took off after it invested in lake living. That growth means most houses here are from the last 25 years, many of them two-story homes with architectural shingle roofs that are now reaching the age of a first replacement or a first big hail claim.

DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofing contractor. One call puts you through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Little Elm calls, and that company does the inspecting, pricing and work.

The Little Elm roofing permit question

People search for a Little Elm roofing permit because the answer is not posted on one simple page. Here is what the town's own material says.

The rule in the code

The building code Little Elm applies says any owner, agent or contractor who wants to alter or repair a building must first apply to the code official and get the required permit for the work.

Who issues it

Building Safety, part of the Development Services Department, reviews, issues and inspects permits. Its office is at 100 West Eldorado Parkway.

Where it is filed

Applications, contractor registrations and yearly registration renewals all run through MyGov, the town's online request center.

How to get a straight answer

Call Building Safety at 214-975-0456 or email permits@littleelm.org with your address and the work planned. Ask before tear-off, not after.

The town's 2020 residential packet listed a $100 contractor registration fee. Fees change, so treat that as a guide and confirm the current amount with the town.

Four reasons Little Elm homeowners call about roofs

The first replacement

Houses built during the 2000s boom are now old enough that their original shingles are wearing out, especially on south and west slopes that take the most afternoon sun.

Hail on March 14, 2024

Reader photos of hail in Little Elm ran on NBC DFW that night, and nearby reports logged stones up to about 2.5 inches. Damage from a storm like that may not show from the street.

Open-water wind

Homes near the shoreline can catch wind that has crossed open water with little to slow it. Wind lifts shingle edges and ridge caps, which later lets rain in.

HOA approval

Many newer neighborhoods have design rules on shingle color and style. Ask the HOA what is approved before signing, so the roofer orders the right product.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before you hire a Little Elm roofing contractor

  • Is your company registered in Little Elm's MyGov system for this year?
  • Will you apply for the permit, and will you send me the permit number?
  • What shingle are you quoting, and is it on my HOA's approved list?
  • How do you handle decking that turns out to be soft once the old roof is off?
  • Can your insurer email me your liability certificate directly?
  • For a hail claim, which storm date do your photos support?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

What happens when you call

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

Hail marks on a 20-year-old roof, a leak after a lake storm, or an HOA letter about a worn roof? Call and explain it. A roofing company that serves Little Elm looks in person and gives you a written figure.

Little Elm roofing questions

Do I need a roofing permit in Little Elm?

Plan on asking for one. The building code Little Elm enforces says anyone who wants to alter or repair a building must first apply for and get the required permit, and the town's Building Safety division issues and inspects those permits through its MyGov portal. The town's pages do not spell out re-roofs on their own, so confirm with Building Safety at 214-975-0456 or permits@littleelm.org before tear-off.

How do I pick a roofing contractor in Little Elm?

Start by asking whether the company is registered with the town; Little Elm handles contractor registrations and yearly renewals in MyGov. Then get a written scope, ask who pulls the permit, request the liability certificate from the company's insurer, and compare at least two estimates. Texas does not license roofers, so these checks carry the weight. More items to request are in the Texas roofer checklist.

Did the March 2024 hail hit Little Elm?

Hail fell across the area on the evening of March 14, 2024. NBC DFW published reader photos labeled as hail in Little Elm, and storm report listings show stones of roughly 1.5 to 2.5 inches within a few miles of town. A roof nobody has checked since that night is worth a professional look. Ask your insurer how long you have to report storm damage.

Are Little Elm roofers part of DFW Expert Roofers?

No. DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofing contractor. An automated assistant answers at any hour, confirms you need roofing help and what is happening, and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that serves Little Elm. That company inspects and prices the work and is paid by you. A referral fee may be paid to the line by that company. How the line works.
